children: The S&P Global France Services PMI rose to 51.4 in September 2026 from 48.0 in the previous month, reaching its highest level since November 2025 and beating market expectations of 48.3, preliminary estimates showed.
The reading signalled a return to expansion in France’s services sector, with activity supported by improving demand and rising sales.
New orders also increased marginally, marking the first improvement in ten months, while outstanding business rose at its fastest pace in nearly three-and-a-half years.
Despite the improvement in activity, employment continued to decline, with private-sector staffing falling for a fifth consecutive month.
Business confidence also weakened, with firms citing higher interest rates, political uncertainty, and international competition.
Meanwhile, price pressures intensified, with input costs and output charges rising at their fastest pace since May, as companies cited higher fuel, energy, metals, and component costs.

title: France Services Activity Rises to 10-Month High
